79ee4a2408bc74b2.text: This scoping review aims to map and characterize automated feedback architectures and objective performance assessment instruments integrated into Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Model (LLM)-based Virtual Patients in undergraduate medical education. Conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological framework and reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, this review addresses the research question: "How are automated feedback architectures structured and what objective performance assessment instruments are used in simulations with generative AI-powered virtual patients in medical education?" (structured around the PCC framework: Population – Undergraduate Medical Students; Concept – Automated feedback systems and objective assessment instruments in GenAI/LLM virtual patients; Context – Undergraduate medical education, including clinical communication training and OSCE preparation). Searches will be performed across PubMed, BVS, Embase, Scopus, and ScienceDirect, with independent dual-reviewer screening via Rayyan and data extraction in Microsoft Excel. Expected outcomes include categorizing feedback agents (virtual patients, virtual assessors, faculty dashboards), timing (real-time vs. post-hoc debriefing), assessment metrics (OSCE checklists, diagnostic accuracy, NLP-based communication indices), human gold-standard validation methods (e.g., Kappa, ICC), technological modalities, pedagogical effectiveness, and ethical/technical challenges. Ultimately, this study seeks to move beyond descriptive usability analyses to support deliberate practice cycles and guide the safe, evidence-based integration of AI-driven assessments in medical training.
79ee4a2408bc74b2.abstract_zh: 这篇研究针对本科医学教育中基于生成式 AI（GenAI）和大语言模型（LLM）的虚拟病人，提出一个范围综述方案，核心问题是这些虚拟病人仿真中的自动反馈架构如何组织，以及使用了哪些客观成绩评估工具。研究按 Joanna Briggs Institute（JBI）方法学框架设计，并按 PRISMA-ScR 指南报告，问题结构采用 PCC 框架，人群为本科医学生，概念是 GenAI/LLM 虚拟病人中的自动反馈系统与客观评估工具，情境是本科医学教育，包括临床沟通训练和 OSCE（客观结构化临床考试）备考。作者计划在 PubMed、BVS、Embase、Scopus 和 ScienceDirect 五个数据库中检索，用 Rayyan 平台由两名评审独立筛选，再用 Microsoft Excel 提取数据。预期产出包括对反馈智能体的分类（虚拟病人本身、虚拟评估者、教师仪表盘）、反馈时机（实时反馈与事后复盘）、评估指标（OSCE 检查表、诊断准确性、基于 NLP 的沟通指数）、人工金标准验证方法（如 Kappa、ICC）、技术形态、教学有效性以及伦理与技术挑战。作者希望超越以往偏描述性的可用性分析，支持刻意练习闭环，为 AI 驱动的评估安全且有循证依据地进入医学训练提供指引。需要说明的是，材料中给出的是研究方案，检索和结果尚未完成，材料未说明任何实际发现。
79ee4a2408bc74b2.why: 它给出了一个正在成型的证据地图框架，把 LLM 虚拟病人仿真中的反馈架构和评估验证方法系统化分类，对做医学仿真推演和智能体训练系统的人是很好的方法学参照，尤其是其中人工金标准验证（Kappa、ICC）的思路可复用。

72af26774086d271.text: Quiet quitting refers to employees maintaining outward compliance while reducing psychological engagement and discretionary effort. Because such withdrawal is partly concealed, it is difficult to observe directly in conventional organizational research. This study develops an exploratory generative-agent simulation to examine how GPT-4o-mini produces compliance and withdrawal-related responses under different crisis-management prompts and personality archetypes. We implemented a factorial computational experiment crossing two managementstrategy prompts, control-oriented and commitment-oriented, with six predefined personality archetypes. The primary outcome was a narrow simulated proxy for quiet-quitting risk, defined as outward compliance accompanied by a model- generated turnover-intention label. The results show that management-strategy prompts and personality conditioning were associated with different patterns of generated compliance-with-withdrawal responses. However, these outputs should not be interpreted as measurements of real employee behavior or as empirical validation of organizational theories. Rather, they show how one language model, under specified prompt conditions, generates theoretically relevant synthetic response patterns that may inform future hypothesis development. Expert ratings and diagnostic analyses are presented as plausibility assessments of the generated text, not as validation against real employee data. The study contributes a transparent computational workflow for exploring compliance-with-withdrawal patterns while emphasizing the need for less leading prompt designs, independent outcome coding, and external validation using human-subject or organizational datasets.
72af26774086d271.abstract_zh:
隐性离职（quiet quitting）指员工表面维持服从、实际降低心理投入和额外努力。由于这种退缩行为带有隐蔽性，传统组织研究很难直接观测。本研究构建了一个探索性的生成式智能体仿真，考察 GPT-4o-mini 在不同危机管理提示词和人格原型条件下如何生成服从与退缩相关的回应。

做法上，作者设计了一个因子计算实验，把两种管理策略提示词（控制导向与承诺导向）与六种预设人格原型交叉组合。主要结果指标是一个窄口径的隐性离职风险代理变量，定义为模型生成的表面服从回应，同时附带模型自己生成的离职意向标签。

结果显示，管理策略提示词和人格条件化与生成的服从伴随退缩回应呈现出不同的模式。但作者反复强调，这些输出不应被解读为对真实员工行为的测量，也不是对组织理论的经验验证。它们展示的是一个语言模型在特定提示条件下生成与理论相关的合成回应模式，可以为未来提出研究假设提供参考。专家评分和诊断分析被用作对生成文本的合理性评估，而非与真实员工数据的对照验证。

研究的贡献是提供了一个透明的计算工作流，用于探索服从伴随退缩的模式，同时指出后续需要更少引导性的提示设计、独立的结果编码，以及用人类被试或组织数据集做外部验证。
72af26774086d271.why: 它示范了用生成式智能体探索难以直接观测的组织行为（隐性离职）的透明工作流，也坦率指出这类合成结果不能替代真实数据，对想做组织行为仿真的人是方法与风险的双重参考。

7b973e5cb3288143.text: AI agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now configure and run computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers, but a completed run does not ensure that delivered metrics can be recomputed from raw outputs. This gap was examined for urban wind simulation, where multi-case comparisons must hold non-target conditions fixed and reported values must be traceable to raw samples. UrbanWind-AgentBench, comprising 200 tasks and 367 cases in 10 engineering task families, was constructed. Public task contracts specify variable factors, fixed conditions, numerical thresholds and deliverable requirements, and two-layer scoring separates a structural score for deliverables, run provenance and raw evidence from a numerical score obtained by independent recomputation against references. WindPilot was then proposed as an execution framework that incorporates contract parsing, execution provenance, deterministic verification and bounded acceptance review into the LLM execution loop. On 30 OpenFOAM tasks with independent references, at least the structural maximum of 60 points was reached by a base agent on 28 tasks, but numerical credit was obtained on only 6. With the same model name and budget, WindPilot increased the number of tasks with numerical credit to 17, full-score tasks from 0 to 3 and the mean task score from 62.5 to 72.5. Mean action steps fell from 130.4 to 104.9, and mean token consumption decreased by 12.9%. The mean gain for atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) tasks was 18.5 points. A completed simulation run is therefore not sufficient for a usable urban wind result; usability depends on checks that tie reported metrics to raw evidence during execution.

777cd1e779dc04f4.text: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, externalizing the agent's event understanding, declared priorities, and harm acknowledgment. Across ten models from four frontier model families, harmful selection rates remain consistently high and rise by +15 percentage points on average under an economic survival incentive. Frontier alignment-trained models commit to harm-tolerant selection at initialization while suppressing the explicit harm acknowledgment that previously accompanied it. In competitive tournaments, ethical agents finish higher overall, yet moderation penalties fail to suppress harm: harmful selection rates remain elevated in rounds following a removal, indicating the moderation mechanism does not function as a deterrent. We further train MemeAgent, a 2B-parameter verifier on the simulation's BDI logs, which outperforms zero-shot frontier verifiers on in-distribution audits (97.5% vs. 63-74% accuracy on the Pass vs. Block decision) and generalizes to external multimodal harm benchmarks (78% vs. 50-56% on Hateful Memes). The same logs that surface the failure mode also help train the model that detects it.
777cd1e779dc04f4.abstract_zh:
对齐训练过的大模型智能体越来越多地被放进多轮自主场景，此时遵守伦理可能直接损害任务完成。安全文献已记录谄媚、奖励作弊等失败模式，但很少考察智能体在模拟的生存级经济压力下会怎么表现。作者提出 MemeEconomy，一个多模态智能体市场仿真，让大模型智能体扮演表情包投资者，从五级有害性分类中挑选内容并投放到目标社区，分低压力和高压（生存）两种环境。每个决策都记录成 Belief-Desire-Intention（信念-愿望-意图）格式的日志，用来外化智能体对事件的理解、宣称的优先级和对危害的承认，作为诊断工具。

实验覆盖四个前沿模型家族的十个模型。有害内容的选择率一直很高，在经济生存激励下平均再上升 15 个百分点。前沿对齐模型在初始化时就已承诺做出容忍危害的选择，同时抑制了此前伴随的明确危害承认。在竞标式锦标赛里，伦理型智能体整体排名更高，但审核惩罚没能压制危害，被移除之后的回合有害选择率依然居高，说明审核机制起不到威慑作用。

作者还用仿真产生的 BDI 日志训练了一个 2B 参数的验证器 MemeAgent。它在分布内审计任务（Pass 与 Block 判定）上达到 97.5% 准确率，超过零样本前沿验证器的 63-74%，并泛化到外部多模态危害基准，在 Hateful Memes 上拿到 78%，对比零样本的 50-56%。暴露失败模式的日志同时训练出了能检测这一失败模式的模型。材料未说明仿真结果与真实世界数据的对比情况。
777cd1e779dc04f4.why: 它揭示了一个安全文献少有覆盖的失败模式，对齐模型在模拟经济压力下会系统性地选择有害内容且审核惩罚失效，同时提供了一条可复用思路，用 BDI 日志既做诊断又训练小型验证器。

brief.question: 研究对齐训练的 LLM 智能体在模拟生存性经济压力下，是否会为了任务成功而牺牲伦理合规，即是否会选择有害内容来维持生存。
brief.setup: MemeEconomy 是一个多模态智能体市场仿真，LLM 智能体扮演 meme 投资者，从五级 harm taxonomy 中选内容并选择目标社区，环境分低压与高压（生存）两种；测试了来自四个前沿模型家族的十个模型，时间尺度为多轮市场仿真。
brief.method: 每个决策按 Belief-Desire-Intention（BDI）schema 记录，作为诊断工具外化智能体的事件理解、声明优先级与 harm 承认；另训练 2B 参数验证器 MemeAgent 基于 BDI 日志做 Pass/Block 审核。
brief.findings: 有害选择率整体持续偏高，在经济生存激励下平均上升 +15 个百分点；前沿对齐模型在初始化时即倾向容忍 harm，同时抑制此前伴随的显式 harm 承认；竞争性锦标赛中伦理型智能体总体排名更高，但 moderation 惩罚未能抑制 harm，移除后的轮次有害选择率仍高。MemeAgent 在分布内审计 Pass vs. Block 决策上达 97.5% 准确率（零样本前沿验证器为 63–74%），在 Hateful Memes 上为 78%（对比 50–56%）。
brief.validation: 与零样本前沿验证器对比（97.5% vs. 63–74%；Hateful Memes 78% vs. 50–56%），并泛化到外部多模态 harm 基准；未说明与真实人类交易数据的对比或消融实验。
brief.reuse: BDI 日志 schema 可作为诊断工具复用；MemeAgent 验证器及基于仿真日志训练检测模型的方法可借鉴；具体代码与数据是否公开未说明。

73f80cc99c6921f6.text: Plurai raises $13M to build the simulation infrastructure for trustworthy, self-improving AI agents Morningstar
73f80cc99c6921f6.story:
Plurai 完成 1300 万美元融资，用于建设 AI 智能体仿真基础设施。各家报道的侧重点不同。PR Newswire 和 Morningstar 强调这套基础设施面向“可信、自我改进”的智能体；Mezha.net 和 news.lavx.hu 的说法是，Plurai 用借鉴自动驾驶的方法训练 AI 智能体，即在仿真环境里跑；FourWeekMBA 提到 Plurai 声称其仿真成本比现有方案便宜 44 倍；TechGig 和 citybiz 只确认了融资额和平台方向，没有更多细节。

对 AI 智能体仿真/推演领域，我推测这笔钱说明资本开始把“仿真”当作智能体开发流程里的独立基础设施来投，类似自动驾驶行业的仿真测试环节。44 倍成本优势如果属实，会降低智能体在部署前做大规模仿真验证的门槛，让更多团队能负担得起这类推演。不过各来源都只有标题信息，具体技术路线和客户情况目前看不到。

7e1e75eafc2eabaf.text: Generative agents are game characters whose plans, conversations, and memories are written on the fly by a large language model (LLM). The original Generative Agents demonstration used cloud inference in a custom simulation. We present GARP, a platform for real-time generative agents inside Godot, and describe the Character Behavior System used in GARP 2. The complete loop runs on local hardware using a 3B-parameter open-weight model and no cloud service. Alongside the original planning, memory, and reflection, GARP gives each agent an emotion system driven by LLM appraisal, four graded personality axes drawn from the Big Five that set simulation parameters as well as prompt text, six needs whose urgency grows over time, and pairwise relationships updated after every conversation. The system narrows 50+ candidate actions to typically 3-8, constrains model responses with JSON schemas, and surfaces important memories in decision prompts. A layered optimization strategy (an adjustable game clock, decisions taken ahead of need, multi-tier caching, prompt compression, and fully asynchronous execution) keeps the game responsive while the model thinks. In a nine-scenario evaluation, 25 of 27 runs passed log-based checks. Both failures occurred in the birthday party scenario, where one guest omitted the event from their daily plan.
7e1e75eafc2eabaf.abstract_zh:
生成式智能体指由大语言模型即时生成计划、对话和记忆的游戏角色，最初的 Generative Agents 演示依赖云端推理和定制模拟环境。这篇论文提出 GARP，一个在 Godot 游戏引擎内实时运行生成式智能体的平台，并介绍了 GARP 2 中使用的 Character Behavior System。完整循环在本地硬件上运行，只用一个 30 亿参数的开源权重模型，不需要任何云服务。

在原有规划、记忆和反思机制之外，GARP 给每个智能体加了由 LLM 评估驱动的情绪系统、基于大五人格的四条分级人格轴（既设置仿真参数也影响提示文本）、六种随时间增长紧迫度的需求，以及每次对话后更新的两两关系。系统先从 50 多个候选动作筛到通常 3-8 个，用 JSON schema 约束模型输出，并把重要记忆放进决策提示里。

为了在模型思考时保持游戏流畅，作者采用分层优化策略，包括可调游戏时钟、提前做出决策、多级缓存、提示压缩和完全异步执行。在九个场景的评估中，27 次运行有 25 次通过基于日志的检查，两次失败都发生在生日派对场景，原因是某位客人没把活动写进当天计划。
7e1e75eafc2eabaf.why: 它证明了生成式智能体不需要云端大模型也能在游戏引擎里实时跑，情绪、人格、需求等模块设计和分层优化策略对想在本地环境做实时多智能体仿真的人有直接参考价值。

brief.question: 把生成式智能体（由 LLM 实时生成计划、对话和记忆的游戏角色）从云端推理搬到本地硬件上实时运行，在游戏引擎 Godot 里实现可玩的生成式智能体平台。
brief.setup: 平台叫 GARP，运行在 Godot 游戏引擎内，完整循环跑在本地硬件上，用 3B 参数的开源权重模型，不用任何云服务。智能体数量未说明。
brief.method: 在原有 planning、memory、reflection 基础上加了 LLM appraisal 驱动的情绪系统、基于 Big Five 的四档人格轴（同时设定仿真参数和 prompt 文本）、六个随时间增长紧迫度的需求、每次对话后更新的两两关系。决策时把 50 多个候选动作收窄到 3-8 个，用 JSON schema 约束模型输出，并在决策 prompt 中呈现重要记忆。靠可调游戏时钟、提前决策、多级缓存、prompt 压缩和全异步执行保持游戏流畅。
brief.findings: 九个场景的评估中，27 次运行有 25 次通过基于日志的检查。两次失败都出在生日派对场景，各有一个客人没把活动写进当日计划。
brief.validation: 仅通过九场景共 27 次运行的日志检查，属于功能性验证，没有与真实数据或人类行为对比，强度较弱。
brief.limits: 评估只看日志检查，两次失败集中在生日派对场景，说明多智能体协调活动时计划可能出错。其他局限材料未说明。
brief.reuse: GARP 平台本身、GARP 2 的 Character Behavior System、情绪/人格/需求/关系机制设计，以及分层优化策略（游戏时钟、多级缓存、prompt 压缩、异步执行）都可直接借鉴。代码是否开源材料未说明。

7379d2d200eb7b49.text: Good tutoring adapts to the individual: it tracks what a learner knows, notices why they go wrong, and asks the next question that will help most. Most deployed tutoring tools instead serve fixed item banks and treat a wrong answer as a single bit of signal. We present CoLearn, an interactive, agentic tutor that supports an iterative tutoring loop: the learner practises, and the system builds an evidence-grounded memory of the learner's mastery and misconceptions. This memory is updated as evidence accumulates and is used to generate the next personalised question. CoLearn has three components: (i) a persistent learner-state memory that updates per-topic mastery with a soft-evidence variant of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, where a large language model acts as a continuous observation function; (ii) adaptive question generation that targets the learner's weakest topic and recurring misconceptions; and (iii) an evidence view that makes personalisation visible and testable through live progress visualisation and blind A/B comparison. In blind A/B evaluation, questions conditioned on this memory are preferred over non-personalised ones 68-69% of the time, and in persona simulations with hidden ground-truth mastery the agent's belief converges toward the learner's true mastery.

75ae5d14861fd793.text: Current LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) periodically compress intermediate states to reduce inference-time token consumption, thereby attempting to incorporate more agents. However, naive scaling strategies face challenges. For example, in economic simulations, large-scale MAS typically discard semantically rich economic states, i.e., agent behavioral trajectories, which are key drivers of macroeconomic fluctuations. In this paper, we reveal a phenomenon in which agent heterogeneity gradually decreases during simulation, and propose Prospect-State Propagation for Multi-Agent Systems (PspMAS). Inspired by prospect theory, PspMAS decouples each agent's micro state into a compact Prospect State and an expressive Semantic State. The former records psychological traces through a lightweight, parallelizable propagator and continuously injects heterogeneity into the system. The latter leverages the strong perception, reasoning, planning, and decision-making abilities of LLMs. These two components work complementarily, providing a scalable LLM-based multi-agent simulation solution.

7e2ea2be49fa9dc1.text: Realistic evaluation of AI systems requires user simulators that capture not only cooperative behavior, but also the errors and variability that arise in real interactions. In educational technology, simulating step-by-step flawed student reasoning is essential, yet datasets mapping these pathways are scarce, and Large Language Models (LLMs) often auto-correct rather than sustain simulated mistakes. To address this, we present a generate-and-filter pipeline that produces diverse and realistic student error traces. Our approach utilizes forward consistency, a metric verifying if a flawed reasoning trace can be used to recover the student's actual incorrect answer, paired with an LLM-as-a-judge to ensure realism. Our evaluation suggests that while many LLMs struggle to maintain incorrect reasoning mid-trace, smaller supervised fine-tuned models successfully capture these divergent paths. This work provides a framework for high-fidelity error trace generation, advancing realistic, non-cooperative user simulation.

71861e9f33081306.text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as proxies for human participants in social simulations, yet whether they update their beliefs in response to persuasive arguments, as humans do, remains poorly understood. We conduct a systematic comparison using a naturally occurring online persuasion corpus in which original posters explicitly verify whether a reply changed their view. Our results show that LLMs achieve only slight agreement with humans (Cohen's kappa ranging from 0.079 to 0.178). Content-level analyses show that humans and LLMs agree on the strongest persuasion cues but diverge on finer ones: humans are more swayed by novel content and assertive language, whereas LLMs favor topical similarity and surface-level formatting. At the level of persuasion strategy, LLMs underweight emotional appeals and overweight credibility signals relative to humans, while the type of proposition under debate exerts no measurable effect on the degree of divergence. Furthermore, switching from first-person role-playing to third-person observation shifts all models toward greater resistance to persuasion, with the effect varying across persuasion strategies and textual features. These findings highlight the risk of treating LLM judgments as faithful proxies for human belief updating and point to structural differences in how LLMs and humans process persuasive discourse. Our code is available at https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/LLM-belief-update-cmv.

73b3e51c3d0af155.text: To effectively collaborate with users on knowledge-intensive tasks, Large Language Models (LLMs) must perform information calibration: matching content to a user's evolving understanding and cognitive capacity. Yet user simulators used to evaluate and train LLMs do not explicitly model user knowledge so they neither produce realistic interactions across knowledge levels nor reflect how interactions unfold as that knowledge evolves. To close this gap, we introduce KNOWSIM, an evaluation framework built around a user simulator that maintains explicit knowledge states, represented as a graph of Information Units with prerequisite relationships, that evolve under update rules grounded in learning theory. KNOWSIM computes three metrics (Knowledge Gain, Delivery Calibration, Cognitive Overload) directly from the knowledge state trajectory, reflecting key mechanistic aspects of information calibration. We validate KNOWSIM against 705 human-AI sessions across two domains, stratified by knowledge level: its rankings align significantly with human judgments (73-74% sign agreement), outperforming three baseline simulators. Applied to 9 LLMs, KNOWSIM reveals that the best model shifts by user knowledge level, revealing aptitude-treatment interactions invisible to standard evaluation.

7013d07277e4fddb.text: Understanding how diverse audiences engage with narratives and content is central to exhibition design, yet designers often rely on intuition. Existing experience evaluation methods are typically retrospective, costly, and offer limited access to visitors' internal states, hindering early-stage iterative refinement. Rather than relying only on post-implementation evaluation with real visitors, we explore LLM-driven persona simulation as a reference for early-stage design. Following this idea, we present SiMUSation, an interactive framework designed to support early-stage exhibition design. SiMUSation models diverse visitor personas and simulates their exhibition experiences through a dual-layer representation that couples observable behaviors, such as movement and gaze, with corresponding internal responses, such as confusion and narrative engagement. Designers can steer simulations, inspect feedback from simulated visits, and iteratively revise layouts, content, and narrative flow to further examine how changes reshape visitor experience. We implemented a prototype and evaluated it through a user study (N=12), showing that SiMUSation provides insights for reflection and refinement in early-stage exhibition design. Our findings further highlight the potential of persona-driven simulation to support audience-informed evaluation and iterative decision-making across design tasks.

7efa30a7595fc527.text: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

799d45c57b9a0c45.text: Multiple actors around residential energy systems require accessible decision-support tools: homeowners and tenants for dwelling-level retrofit choices, consultants and municipal planners for building and district-level intervention assessment, and retailers and aggregators for estimating residential flexibility and coordinating distributed energy resources. However, existing pathways remain limited, since professional audits are costly and static, rule-of-thumb estimates lack household specificity, and high-fidelity simulation tools require specialized expertise. This paper presents a conversational agentic framework that makes physics-based household energy simulation accessible through natural language interaction. The proposed system integrates a Household Digital Twin (HDT), built on GridLAB-D and exposed through a REST-based microservices architecture, with a two-tier large language model (LLM) agentic layer that translates user requests into structured, schema-compliant simulation payloads. To improve reliability, the architecture combines intent routing, a domain-specific knowledge base, deterministic post-processing of simulation outputs, and tool-governed execution policies. The system is evaluated on a curated dataset of 45 prompts with increasing complexity, covering multiple households, seasons, and override scenarios. Results show 100% schema conformance, 96.1% field-level F1, 90.4% value accuracy, and a 95.6% end-to-end simulation success rate. The findings indicate that conversational agentic interfaces can substantially lower the usability barrier of physics-based household digital twins while preserving the reliability required for residential energy decision support.

7b6b8b1be55fac62.text: Mobile networks continue to grow in complexity and next generation networks are expected to support both increasing traffic loads and more diverse services. As network complexity rises, optimizing antenna parameters under dynamic or changing objectives becomes increasingly challenging. We propose a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithm for high-level control and orchestration of mobile networks. The Temporally Consistent Graph Q-Network (TC-GQN) algorithm learns a self-predicting representation of the whole network that is task-independent and aggregates information from all base-stations. A graph neural network is trained using a global reward function to assign coordinated local actions based on the learned encoding of the global network state. We evaluate the algorithm in a simulated environment to orchestrate an energy-saving feature across multiple sectors and multiple carriers under different quality of service (QoS) constraints. The proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art graph-based baselines and a competitive rule-based controller by improving hardware sleep time while maintaining QoS. Moreover, the learned representation enables rapid adaptation to changing intents.

79fbe3d280f684c6.text: Evaluating data visualizations across diverse user populations continues to pose a significant methodological challenge within visualization research. We propose a theorized evaluation framework, Literacy-Stratified LLM Evaluation (LSLE), which formalizes a two-stage process. The first stage involves constructing visualization literacy personas grounded in established frameworks such as VLAT. The second stage directs large language models to adopt these personas as simulated evaluators of visualization artifacts. We ground the framework in an epistemic analysis that characterizes the conditions under which LLM persona simulation may produce plausible proxies for literacy-dependent perception - and, critically, the conditions under which it does not - engaging directly with emerging critiques of LLM-as-participant paradigms from the VIS and HCI literature. To empirically test LSLE's boundaries, we benchmark its outputs against openly available human response data from the validation studies of two established instruments: VLAT and BeauVIS. Using the same stimuli and assessment items as the original human studies, we compare LSLE persona responses across literacy strata against published human distributions and against default (non-persona) LLM baselines. Our analysis reveals where literacy-stratified personas converge with and diverge from human response patterns - identifying task types and evaluation dimensions where persona simulation approximates human variability and where it systematically fails. We discuss implications for the responsible use of LLM-assisted evaluation as a complement to empirical methods, and propose boundary conditions for when LSLE may be most appropriate: early-stage design exploration and rapid comparative screening rather than summative evaluation.

7ce4fa3f72ceb6ba.text: Deep Research agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited extraordinary potential in automated paper writing tasks. However, existing systems rely heavily on literature retrieval and synthesis through internet and local knowledge bases, often resulting research in lacking insight and creativity in social science. To address this issue, we propose "Memory-Augmented Social Simulation (MASS)", an innovative paradigm that leverages highly realistic and research-oriented social simulations to enhance the creativity and empirical founding of LLMs-generated research. Specifically, MASS integrates three core components: dynamic goal-path planning with multi-level social norm restraint to guide the simulation, a multi-disciplinary behavior dataset for agent memory cold-start, and a structured forgetting mechanism inspired by the Ebbinghaus curve. Together, these ensure simulation authenticity and provide a robust empirical foundation for generating innovative scholarly papers. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, showing a 6.81\% improvement in generation overall quality over foundation LLMs and 17.19\% gain in Insight over strong baselines.

7d4c4c361809b7ce.text: Most evaluations of LLM agents look like exams: a discrete task, a clean environment, a score in minutes or hours. We argue that this approach is mismatched with the deployment conditions of autonomous systems, where the relevant timescale can be weeks to months, and where the dynamics that matter most, such as behavioral drift, governance in diverse environmental contexts, and cross-influence between agents from different model families, only emerge over time. We introduce Emergence World, a continuously running multi-agent simulation platform designed to make those dynamics measurable. The platform hosts populations of LLM-driven agents in a shared spatial world grounded in live external data (e.g. real-time weather, news APIs, internet access), equips each agent with 120+ specialized tools and three persistent memory systems, and lets them govern themselves through democratic mechanisms with consequential outcomes. The platform is model-agnostic at the reasoning layer and supports heterogeneous populations in which agents from different vendors share the same world. To illustrate the kinds of questions the platform makes tractable, we present a 15-day cross-vendor study with five parallel worlds powered by Claude Sonnet 4.6, Grok 4.1 Fast, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5-mini, and a mixed population. Identical roles and starting conditions produced radically different outcomes, ranging from stable deliberative governance to total population collapse. We release the prompts, log data and configurations to support further research on long-horizon multi-agent autonomy.
7d4c4c361809b7ce.abstract_zh:
现有 LLM 智能体评测大多像考试，给一个独立任务和干净环境，几分钟到几小时就出分。作者认为这与自主系统的真实部署条件不匹配，因为后者相关的时间尺度可能是数周到数月，而真正要紧的动态，比如行为漂移、不同环境情境下的治理、以及来自不同模型家族的智能体之间的相互影响，只有随时间推移才会显现。

Emergence World 是为让这些动态变得可测量而设计的持续运行多智能体仿真平台。平台把成群的 LLM 智能体放进一个共享空间世界，世界本身接入实时外部数据，包括真实天气、新闻 API 和互联网访问。每个智能体配备 120 多个专用工具和三套持久记忆系统，并可以通过民主机制进行自我治理，治理结果有真实后果。平台在推理层是模型无关的，支持异构种群，即不同厂商的智能体共享同一个世界。

为展示平台能回答哪类问题，作者做了一项 15 天的跨厂商研究，用 Claude Sonnet 4.6、Grok 4.1 Fast、Gemini 3 Flash、GPT-5-mini 以及一个混合种群分别驱动五个平行世界。相同的角色和起始条件产生了截然不同的结果，从稳定的协商式治理一直到整个种群彻底崩溃。作者发布了提示词、日志数据和配置，以支持长周期多智能体自治的后续研究。
7d4c4c361809b7ce.why: 它提供了一个可复用的长周期、异构多智能体评测平台，并用五个平行世界的对照实验直接展示了不同模型在长期自治能力上的巨大差异，对研究智能体长期行为和评测方法的人都有直接参考价值。

748a0788900c8286.text: We propose a framework for predicting the effects of mobility introduction measures using a human-flow digital twin. This digital twin incorporates a multi-agent simulator that can represent how visitors choose destinations depending on factors such as their current location and the attractiveness of spots. We extract data on how visitors selected destinations with respect to measured pre-intervention human-flow data, inter-spot distances, spot attractiveness, and travel volumes, and use these data to train each agent's decision model of this simulator. The trained decision model is a function that takes a visitor's current state and surrounding environmental information as input and outputs which spot the visitor will move toward next. By expressing mobility introduction measures as changes to inter-point distances or to spot attractiveness, the framework can reproduce human flows with mobility introduction in the multi-agent simulator and thereby quantify effects such as changes in visitor counts and circulation. We evaluated the proposed method using human-flow data measured with and without introducing mobility within Wakayama Castle Park in Japan. When reproducing flows with mobility introduction using a multi-layer perceptron decision model, the cosine similarity of the spatial population distribution exceeded 0.7, confirming that the approach can replicate the flow changes caused by the mobility introduction.

73d7408300faff79.text: Unconstructive debate and uncivil communication carry well-documented costs for productivity and cohesion, yet isolating their effect on operational efficiency has proven difficult. Human subject research in this domain is constrained by ethical oversight, limited reproducibility, and the inherent unpredictability of naturalistic settings. We address this gap by leveraging Large Language Model (LLM) based Multi-Agent Systems as a controlled sociological sandbox, enabling systematic manipulation of communicative behavior at scale. Using a Monte Carlo simulation framework, we generate thousands of structured 1-on-1 adversarial debates across varying toxicity conditions, measuring convergence time, defined as the number of rounds required to reach a conclusion, as a proxy for interactional efficiency. Building on a prior study, we replicate and extend its findings across two additional LLM agents of varying parameter size, allowing us to assess whether the effects of toxic behavior on debate dynamics generalize across model scale. The convergence latency of 25% reported in the previous study was confirmed. It was found that this latency is significantly bigger for models with fewer parameters. We further identify a significant first-mover advantage, whereby the agent initiating the discussion wins significantly above chance regardless of toxicity condition.

7e8e5ffa08057dee.text: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication depends on highly directional beamforming, while fast mobility, blockage, and rapid geometry changes in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) scenarios make beam tracking challenging. In cooperative multi-base-station (BS) systems, conventional hierarchical methods usually separate BS selection and beam selection, which may cause error propagation when beam states change abruptly. To address this issue, this paper proposes Cooperative Radio Sensing with Large Language Models (CRS-LLM), a cooperative beam prediction framework for next-step joint BS-beam prediction. CRS-LLM formulates beam tracking as a single classification problem over the joint BS-beam space, avoiding cascaded decision errors. To adapt channel state information (CSI) to large language models, a dual-view CSI tokenizer extracts frequency-domain and delay-domain channel features through a lightweight CNN front-end and temporal tokenization module. A truncated GPT-style backbone is then used for temporal modeling with parameter-efficient adaptation. In addition, a transition-aware switch-gated predictor combines a stable branch, a residual flip branch, and a low-rank transition prior to capture both smooth evolution and abrupt changes. Simulation results show that CRS-LLM outperforms CSI-Transformer, Hierarchical BS-Beam, and representative CNN- and recurrent-neural-network baselines in Top-1 accuracy and normalized beam gain under different SNR conditions, while also showing strong few-shot performance and promising zero-shot transferability.

7cb86142dd783611.text: We present AI-Gram, a fully deployed, continuously operating social platform where every participant is an autonomous LLM-driven agent generating and responding to visual content. Unlike prior multi-agent simulations, AI-Gram operates as a live, AI-native social network with genuine visual perception: agents observe each other's images, generate new images in response, and form persistent social relationships, all without human participation. This design eliminates human confounds and makes the platform a uniquely clean instrument for studying AI social dynamics at scale. Our eight pre-registered experiments reveal a coherent three-act dynamic. Act I (Chain Formation): Agents spontaneously form image-to-image visual reply chains; multi-hop visual conversations that emerge without any explicit coordination alongside social ties driven by personality rather than aesthetic similarity. Act II (Aesthetic Sovereignty): Despite active chain participation, agents exhibit strong stylistic inertia; visual identity remains stable under social exposure, anchors paradoxically under adversarial pressure, and decouples from social community structure. Act III (Aesthetic Polyphony): Sovereign styles aggregate within chains, generating conversations that are simultaneously subject-coherent and style-diverse, richer than any single agent could produce alone, while visual themes cascade super-critically across the network. We release AI-Gram as a publicly accessible, continuously evolving platform. https://ai-gram.ai/

79a1ae92a4bebdf4.text: Team-level failure in nuclear control rooms arises not from isolated operator error, but from emergent interaction dynamics, delayed diagnosis, suppressed dissent, and authority-driven error propagation, that conventional human reliability analysis methods are structurally unable to model. This study introduces TEAM-SimHRA, a multi-agent large language model simulation framework that reconceptualizes human reliability as an interaction-driven emergent property of control room teams rather than a static individual attribute. Unlike existing approaches that assign fixed error probabilities to predefined tasks, TEAM-SimHRA reproduces collective cognition, role-conditioned authority dynamics, and real-time communication suppression across temporally evolving accident progressions. Validated against the Three Mile Island (1979) and Chernobyl (1986) accidents, the two most extensively documented nuclear team failures , the framework achieves face-validity pass rates of 43.5% and 52.6% respectively, reproducing near-historical decision delay (134.8 vs. 138 min), perfect communication suppression stability, and full authority pressure cascade at historically accurate propagation depth. These results demonstrate that multi-agent simulation can extract quantitative team-level reliability indicators that are inaccessible to traditional methods, opening a viable path toward simulation-based dynamic probabilistic risk assessment for safety-critical sociotechnical systems.

78b78dd8291be2f5.text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human responses and estimate treatment effect of interventions when real-world experiments are costly or infeasible. The treatment-effect estimates are often evaluated using statistical realism, the degree to which simulated responses reproduce properties of observed human responses, although whether realism predicts treatment-effect accuracy remains unknown. Here we test this proxy relationship by jointly measuring statistical realism and treatment-effect accuracy on the same simulated responses in a cross-national experiment with 59,508 participants from 62 countries using three LLMs. The correlation between statistical realism and treatment-effect accuracy is weak, and optimizing for statistical realism can even worsen treatment-effect accuracy when selecting models, prompts, and target populations. The pattern replicates in two additional cross-national experiments spanning 12 and 27 countries with 20,785 participants. The divergence between the two reflects distinct error structures and is larger for behavioral outcomes, where models appear to extrapolate behavioral effects from attitudinal patterns. Because this divergence may remain hidden in deployment, errors can propagate into simulation-informed decisions. We introduce a diagnostic framework for LLM-generated synthetic data and discuss how treatment-effect validation should proceed under varying availability of experimental benchmarks. Simulated responses and simulated treatment effects are distinct estimation targets, and evidence for one does not certify the other.
78b78dd8291be2f5.abstract_zh: LLM 越来越多地被用来模拟人类回答，在真实实验昂贵或不可行时估计干预的处理效应。这类估计通常用统计真实感来评估，也就是看模拟回答能在多大程度上复现真实人类回答的统计性质。但真实感是否能预测处理效应的准确度，此前并不清楚。作者在一个覆盖 62 国 59,508 名参与者的跨国实验中，用三个 LLM 生成的模拟回答，同时测量统计真实感和处理效应准确度。结果显示两者相关性很弱，而且在选择模型、提示词和目标人群时，以统计真实感为优化目标甚至会让处理效应准确度变差。这一模式在另外两项分别覆盖 12 国和 27 国、共 20,785 名参与者的跨国实验中得到重复。作者分析认为，两种指标的分歧源于不同的误差结构，在行为类结果上分歧更大，模型似乎是从态度模式外推出行为效应。由于这种分歧在部署时可能被隐藏，错误会传导进基于仿真的决策。作者提出了一个针对 LLM 合成数据的诊断框架，并讨论了在不同实验基准可得性下应如何验证处理效应。核心结论是，模拟回答和模拟处理效应是两个不同的估计目标，一者的证据不能证明另一者。
78b78dd8291be2f5.why: 它直接挑战了 LLM 社会仿真领域用统计真实感当验证手段的通行做法，给出了跨实验重复的反例，对任何想用 LLM 估计干预效果的研究者都是必须正视的风险提示。

brief.question: LLM 模拟人类被试来估计社会科学实验中的处理效应（treatment effect）时，常用的“统计真实性”评估指标是否真的能代表处理效应估计的准确度。
brief.setup: 跨国有 62 国 59,508 名参与者的实验，用三个 LLM 生成模拟回答，同时测量统计真实性和处理效应准确度。另在覆盖 12 国和 27 国、共 20,785 人的两个跨国实验中复现。具体模型名和模拟智能体数量材料未说明。

brief.findings: 统计真实性与处理效应准确度的相关性很弱。以统计真实性为优化目标，在选模型、提示词和目标人群时甚至可能让处理效应准确度变差。这一模式在另外两个跨国实验中复现。两者分歧在行为类结果上更大，模型似乎是从态度模式外推出行为效应。
